findings.reason: Confirmed, though I would grade it medium rather than high: the false sentence is an explanation, and no item statement or build instruction changes. He21 fixes the base alcove in the chamber opposite the dominant one (arXiv:2001.03325 p.5, '…the dominant Weyl chamber of V is opposite to the unique Weyl chamber containing a'), with critical strips −1 < ⟨v,α⟩ < 0 for positive α. Translations then act by v ↦ v − λ. This is the only sign for which t^λ ∈ ^S W̃ for dominant λ, and for which the paper's ℓ(xt^λ) = ℓ(x) + ℓ(t^λ) (p.10) holds; I checked the latter in A_1. The E1 example of the extraction also behaves as stated under this sign. I reran the construction of the proof of Theorem 5.5 (pp.10–11) for split adjoint A_2 with λ_w = 2ω_2^∨, x = s_1, y = s_2. t^λ s_2 ∈ ^S W̃ because s_2(α_1) > 0, and supp(η(w)) = supp(s_2s_1) = S. The construction gives J = {s_2}, ρ^∨_J = ω_2^∨, J′ = {s_1}, s_2s_1 = x′z with x′ = s_2 and z = s_1, γ = dominant(ω_2^∨ + s_2ω_2^∨) = ω_1^∨, K = {s_2}, y′ = 1, and a = s_1 ∗ s_2 = s_1s_2. In root coordinates (⟨·,α_1⟩, ⟨·,α_2⟩), a t^γ maps the base-alcove vertices (0,0), (−1,0), (0,−1) to (1,−1), (2,−2), (2,−1). The values of α_1, α_2 and α_1+α_2 then lie in [1,2], [−2,−1] and [0,1], so the alcove meets no critical strip and is shrunken. Yet γ is a nonzero singular coweight and supp(a) = S. E1's argument fails because ⟨v, a(α)⟩ ∈ (−1,0) is a critical strip only when a(α) is positive, and here a(α_2) = −(α_1+α_2). So E1's universal claim 'not shrunken whenever γ is not regular' is false; it is correct only as an existential statement, as E1's own λ = ω_2^∨ example shows. The gap verdict of E1 and the GHN15 Theorem A repair are unaffected, and item /120 already imposes no shrunken hypothesis. The fix is right, with one addition: gap G3's detail repeats the universal claim ('whose hypothesis the constructed a t^γ does not satisfy whenever γ is not regular') and must be reworded the same way. Its instruction to plan the seed from GHN15 Theorem A or the class-polynomial route stays.

Confirmed (medium). The GHN15 erratum (https://www.esaga.uni-due.de/f/ulrich.goertz/pdf/Erratum-GHN.pdf, SHA-256 cf7efbf8…99c0, the copy E13 cites) states Proposition 0.0.1 for general G on p.1. Its kernel calculation on p.2 opens with 'Assume that G is semisimple. In this case the map π_0(Flag) → π_0(Flag_ad) is injective if and only if the coinvariants X_*(T)_Γ are torsion-free', and identifies the kernel with X_*(T)_{Γ,tors} under that assumption. E13's reason and its embedded review state both the kernel formula and the 'exactly when torsion-free' criterion without the hypothesis. For general reductive G that is false. For split GL_2, X_*(T)_Γ = Z² is torsion-free, but π_0(Flag) = π_1(GL_2) = Z maps onto π_1(PGL_2) = Z/2 with kernel 2Z. Item /104 keeps injectivity as a separate hypothesis, so no item statement is affected. The fix is right: add 'for semisimple G' to both attributions and keep the general componentwise isomorphism.
